setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 has pattern 1 assigned over steps 1 to 4, but pattern 1's trigs have been cleared, so no step is lit. A MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Record is off. The norns clock source is internal; an external MIDI clock at 100 BPM is available. Mosaic records each note onto the step that is playing when the note arrives, so recording needs a running clock: this lesson borrows the external one. If you have no external clock, start Mosaic's own clock with Play (1,8) and arm Record the same way.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, open the CLOCK group and turn E3 so Source reads midi. Mosaic now follows the external 100 BPM clock.
steps.title: Follow the external clock

steps.caption: Close the menu and tap Record (2,8) to arm recording. While the external clock runs, play MIDI note 72 at velocity 90 and then note 79 at velocity 80 on the keyboard. Each note lands on the step playing when it arrives. Tap Record again to disarm. The grid shows steps 2 and 4 lit, and steps 1 and 3 empty. Which steps light depends on when you press, so your own take may land elsewhere.
steps.title: Record two notes

steps.caption: Tap K1, open the CLOCK group and turn E3 back so Source reads internal. Following the external clock left the tempo at 100 BPM, so turn E2 to the tempo row and turn E3 until it reads 90 BPM; any tempo works, the notes' spacing simply follows it.
steps.title: Back to the internal clock at 90 BPM

steps.caption: Close the menu and tap Play (1,8). The channel plays note 72 at velocity 90, then note 79 at velocity 80, repeating, as the MIDI strip lists. The two notes sit on steps 2 and 4, so they alternate every two steps: at 90 BPM with the default Rate /1 that is one third of a second apart.
steps.title: Replay and hear the rhythm
